settings.text_content:
There is a very particular kind of chaos that happens in the 10 minutes before you see someone you have been thinking about since the group chat went suspiciously quiet. You road test three different outfits. A decision about the trainers gets made, then reversed twice. Almost nobody spares a thought for what they are actually going to smell like, which is a shame, because fragrance underpins the laws of attraction more than anyone gives it credit for.


This will not get you cast in the next series of Love Island, but it might be the one detail your situationship remembers about you long after they have forgotten what you were wearing. It also happens to be the one part of the whole process that is actually within your control. Unlike the trainers.

Scent does more than you think it does

Smell is wired straight into the part of the brain that handles memory and emotion, more directly than anything you see or hear. It is the reason a specific fragrance can put you back in a specific kitchen, or a specific car, years after the fact. It is also why most people can tell you exactly what an ex used to wear long after everything else about the relationship has gone hazy. Scent tends to outlast almost everything else in memory, occasionally including the person wearing it. Choose the right fragrance and you end up quietly attaching yourself to someone's memory in a way a good outfit never quite manages.

settings.heading: Work with your own skin, not a stranger's
settings.body_text:
The fragrance that smelled incredible on your friend does not automatically do the same thing on you, and that is not a flaw in the bottle. Skin chemistry, body heat, even your diet all impact how a fragrance actually reads once it is on you rather than on the tester strip. Spray it on your wrist, not the paper, and give it 20 minutes before deciding anything. First impressions from a fragrance counter are almost always
wrong, because you are smelling the top notes, not the version that actually lasts. If you can, wear it for a full day before you commit. A fragrance that still smells like you want it to by early evening is the one worth buying, not the one that impressed you for ten minutes after you spritzed all over in Boots.

settings.heading: Addiction vs Baccarat Rouge 540: the one everyone argues about
settings.column_1_text: Baccarat Rouge 540 by Maison Francis Kurkdjian is, at this point, a cultural phenomenon. It retails at around £270 for 70ml from the MFK counter at Harrods or Liberty. It smells like nothing else: jasmine, saffron, ambergris, and cedar with a quality that is warm and faintly synthetic in the best possible way. It became the most talked-about fragrance of the last decade because it smells like nothing that came before it. There is a reason every perfume lover in the country has a strong opinion about it.
settings.column_2_text:
Addiction, our version inspired by Baccarat Rouge 540, opens in the same territory. The saffron and jasmine are immediately there, and the amber and cedar base develops in a way that tracks closely with the original throughout the day. The dry-down is where differences between inspired fragrances and originals most often show up, and here the gap is narrow. The warmth is there. That particular quality that makes the original so memorable, the slightly sweet, slightly metallic depth, comes through.

The biggest practical difference: Addiction is a couple of tenners. Baccarat Rouge 540 is £270. Both lasted a full day on moisturised skin in our test. The inspired version does not come with the Kurkdjian brand experience, the weighty glass bottle, or the knowledge that your fragrance costs more than most weekly Tesco food shops for a family of 4. What it does come with is the scent, which is the part you are actually wearing.

settings.heading: Fresh for a first hello, warm for everything after
settings.box_paragraph_1: For someone you are only just getting to know, brighter and cleaner fragrances tend to land better. Citrus, light florals, and anything that reads as fresh rather than heavy comes across as approachable rather than a statement you did not ask them to read. Once things are a bit further along, warmer notes, amber, vanilla, soft musk, sit closer to the skin and read as considerably more personal. This is the difference between a fragrance someone notices and one they end up associating specifically with you.
settings.subheading: For her: Luminous Wonder (inspired by J'Adore by Dior)
settings.bottom_text: J'Adore has built an entire reputation on being the fragrance people lean in to ask about, and Luminous Wonder works from the same instinct. Melon and magnolia open things brightly enough for a first meeting, ylang-ylang and jasmine take over as the evening progresses, and a soft vanilla and cedar base is what actually lingers once you've left the room. It gets remembered for exactly the reasons you would want it to.

settings.heading: For him: Visionary (inspired by Imagination by Louis Vuitton)
settings.box_paragraph_1: Visionary opens with citron and bergamot, properly fresh and nothing to be intimidated by on a first meeting, before moving into neroli and a touch of ginger and settling into black tea and warm cedar. It reads as put together without being flashy about it, which is precisely the impression most people are actually going for and rarely manage.

settings.body_text:
Do not overspray. Two sprays, pulse points, and then leave it alone. A fragrance
somebody has to lean in to properly notice does more work than one that arrives in
the room four minutes before you do. Wear it consistently for a few weeks and something quietly useful happens... it stops being a fragrance you are wearing and starts being the thing people associate specifically with you, which was rather the point.

settings.heading: What makes us different from the other lot
settings.body_text:
Scentspired creates luxury inspired perfumes. Each one is developed to capture the essence of a designer fragrance you already know, using high-quality fragrance oils that perform at the level you expect. Not something that smells roughly similar on the first spray and then disappears by lunch. Something you reach for because it works, lasts, and costs about £15.99. The idea being that you can actually wear it. Every day. Without keeping a tally.

We also believe that incredible scent should not be a privilege. It should be accessible to anyone who wants to feel something when they walk into a room, whatever their budget happens to be. That is the whole point of what we do.

The full Scentspired range lists the notes and concentration for every fragrance, so
you can find the one that ends up doing this particular job for you. Browse the
bestsellers, find the one that actually smells like you, and let it do the rest next time
you see them.
